title: Deep Glow 2 Docs (official manual)
author: Plugin Everything (James Whiffin)
why: Every DG2 control with exact behaviour: Exponential vs Iris mode, Screen vs Add (when to tonemap), chrominance vs luminance threshold, saturation bias, lens dirt, quality presets and the flicker/linear-workflow FAQ; turns DG2 from presets into controlled, non-flickering bloom.

title: Trapcode Shine User Guide (all chapters)
author: Maxon / Red Giant
why: Official Shine reference (source point, ray length, shimmer, boost light, colorize, fractal noise, transfer modes): volumetric light rays through logos and type for idents, with the settings that keep rays from looking cheap.

title: Glow | Effects of After Effects
author: Jake In Motion
why: Jake Bartlett walks through every stock Glow parameter (based-on alpha vs color, threshold/radius/intensity interplay, A&B colors, Glow Operation blend modes, composite original), which is the stock fallback and the starting point for glows that must sit on lighter grounds.

title: Backlighting, Flares, Light Volume (After Effects 7.0 Studio Techniques, ch. 12)
author: Mark Christiansen (via flylib)
why: Canonical roll-your-own light wrap recipe (Silhouette/Stencil Alpha + Fast Blur with Repeat Edge Pixels, Add/Screen at low opacity) plus believable flares and volumetric light; directly sells a cut-out host against a bright backdrop with stock AE.

title: ReelSmart Motion Blur User's Manual (official, OFX edition)
author: RE:Vision Effects
why: Official RSMB reference: Blur Amount 0.5 = 180 deg, Motion Sensitivity vs gloop, FG matte separation and Inv Matte Shrink, premult, frame-duplicate pitfalls, 5%-of-frame reach limit and RSMB Vectors format; exactly what blurring delivered PNG sequences and precomps needs.

title: Time effects (Echo, Pixel Motion Blur, Timewarp, Time Displacement)
author: Adobe Help Center
why: Stock alternatives to RSMB with exact controls: Pixel Motion Blur (shutter control/samples/vector detail) for footage and pre-rendered clips, Echo for streak trails, Timewarp motion-blur settings; the stock path when a layer has no keyframed motion to blur.

title: CINEMATIC Motion Blur | After Effects Tutorial
author: pwnisher
why: Andrew Kramer's trick shown by pwnisher: sandwich RSMB/Force Motion Blur between two Exposure gamma adjustments (0.1 / 10) so blurred highlights keep their brightness like in-camera streaks; fixes washed-out, cheap-looking blur on bright and glowing elements.

title: CC Force Motion Blur | Effects of After Effects
author: Jake In Motion
why: CC Force Motion Blur explained (subframe samples, shutter angle, native vs override) - the quick stock way to add true sub-frame blur to precomps and nested animation where layer switches can't reach.

title: Trapcode Particular User Guide (all 56 chapters)
author: Maxon / Red Giant
why: The full official Particular manual (Designer, multiple systems, emit from parent, every emitter type incl. layer/text/3D model, particle types, physics, fluid, fields, layer maps, lighting/shadowlets, DOF and motion blur); gives agents exact parameter meanings and ranges for hero particle shots.

title: Trapcode Form User Guide (all chapters)
author: Maxon / Red Giant
why: Official Form manual: base forms (grid, strings, 3D model, text/mask), layer maps, audio react, disperse/twist, fractal and spherical fields, shadowlets, motion blur; for living particle grids, logo builds and tech backgrounds.

title: CC Particle Systems II + CC Particle World | Effects of After Effects
author: Jake In Motion
why: 73-minute deep dive by Jake Bartlett on the stock particle engines (CC Particle Systems II and CC Particle World): birth rate, longevity, gravity and physics, textured particles from layers, 3D camera interaction; the no-plugin fallback for sparks, dust and bursts.

title: Trapcode Particular 3 Training | 05: Layer Emitters
author: Maxon Red Giant
why: Official Particular training on Layer emitters: emitting particles from a logo/text layer's pixels and colors, layer sampling modes and layer RGB usage; the core technique for particle logo builds and disintegrations in idents.

title: Dancer to Dust - Trapcode Particular Tutorial
author: Maxon Red Giant
why: Maxon recreates the 'dancer falling to dust' demo: an animated character exported as an OBJ sequence drives Particular's 3D model emitter (emit from faces), with turbulence, the built-in ground plane and parent/child systems, then composited into a photo; the recipe for dissolving or materialising a 3D host.

title: Trapcode Form 3 Training | 06: Layer Maps
author: Maxon Red Giant
why: Official Form training on Layer Maps (color/alpha, displacement, size, fractal strength, disperse maps from precomps); how to drive a particle grid from a logo or gradient for controllable, art-directed particle reveals.

title: Advanced 3D renderer
author: Adobe Help Center
why: What Advanced 3D renders (GLB/GLTF/OBJ/FBX, environment lights, extrusions, Adobe Standard Material) and its Render Options: quality, shadow resolution, casting box size/center, Draft 3D; the settings that decide whether 3D in AE looks premium or noisy.

title: Import and add 3D models to your composition
author: Adobe Help Center
why: Supported 3D formats and the exact import flow for GLB/GLTF/OBJ/FBX models (model settings, scale, decluttered import), so device and product models can be dropped into AE shots without leaving the app.

title: Create realistic reflections and ambient lighting in a 3D scene (environment lights)
author: Adobe Help Center
why: Environment light setup with HDR/EXR or animated comps as sources, environment-light shadows and their exceptions, Accepts Lights bypass; image-based lighting is the biggest single jump from flat to photographic 3D in AE.

title: Enable in-engine Depth of Field in Advanced 3D
author: Adobe Help Center
why: AE 26.3's in-engine DOF: Focus Distance linking to a layer, Aperture, Focus Area Width, Near/Far Blur Level, and Render Quality to kill focus-pull ripple; camera-accurate rack focus on models, meshes, text and shapes.

title: Cameras, lights, and points of interest
author: Adobe Help Center
why: Reference for every camera and light setting (focal length/zoom, DOF focus distance, aperture/f-stop, blur level, iris; light types, falloff, shadow darkness/diffusion) and camera commands; the exact values behind premium camera moves and lighting.

title: Build native 3D scenes with meshes and Substance materials
author: Adobe Learn (Jess Libby)
why: AE 2026 parametric meshes plus Substance 3D materials (displacement, subdivision, scale/seam, random seed, keyframed material props), environment light shadow darkness, and the rule that a 2D layer inside a 3D stack breaks lighting and shadows.

title: Professional 3D Renders in After Effects (No plugins!)
author: Jake In Motion
why: Jake Bartlett's full Advanced 3D render workflow with no plugins: Polyhaven HDRIs as environment lights, materials, shadows, render quality settings and finishing passes for photographic 3D product shots.

title: This New Advanced 3D Feature is CRAZY - After Effects Tutorial | 3D Models, HDRI, Shadow Catcher
author: Motion Nations
why: Imports a 3D model, lights it with an HDRI environment light and grounds it on footage with a shadow catcher plane (Accepts Shadows: Only); the native path for compositing a 3D device or object onto a background.

title: Master 3D Glass Effect Motion Graphics in After Effects Advanced Tutorial
author: Stephan Zammit
why: Stephan Zammit builds realistic 3D glass in stock AE: refraction via displacement maps, per-channel dispersion offsets, edge highlights and inner reflections; a premium glassmorphism look for tech promos and logo shapes.

title: Cineware for After Effects
author: Maxon
why: How .c4d scenes load into AE via Cineware: render settings, using C4D cameras, extracting scene data, multi-pass compositing and Live Link; the reference when a Cinema 4D scene (bundled C4D add-on) must be finished in AE.

title: Shadow catchers
author: Adobe Help Center
why: Step-by-step shadow catcher: 3D solid aligned to the ground, Accepts Shadows set to Only, environment light casting, shadow color; grounds a 3D model on a 2D plate so it stops floating.

title: Color Matching (After Effects 7.0 Studio Techniques, ch. 5)
author: Mark Christiansen (via flylib)
why: The channel-by-channel Levels method for matching a foreground to its plate (black/white/midtone references, green first, gamma slamming, Info panel readings); the reliable way to make a host or cut-out sit in the background's light.

title: Shadows and Reflected Light (After Effects 7.0 Studio Techniques, ch. 12)
author: Mark Christiansen (via flylib)
why: Cast shadows from a matte (corner pin, Levels output white 0, luma-matted adjustment layer), the contact-shadow pool trick under feet, and bounce/reflected light; the integration details that stop a composited figure from floating.

title: Advanced Lighting in After Effects
author: Ben Marriott
why: Ben Marriott composites a 2D animated character into a real environment: form shading, cast shadows, highlights, rim light, reactive reflections and shadows that loop with environmental changes; the closest match to grounding our host in a backdrop.

title: Animation Post Production Like a PRO (After Effects Beginner Tutorial)
author: Manu Mercurial
why: Studio-style post-production for 2D animation in AE: story-driven lighting passes, shadows, glows, depth blur to guide the eye, color grade and finishing texture; turns a flat character render into a movie-quality shot.

title: How to Add Soft Shadow Effects to Cartoon Animation Using After Effects
author: Envato Tuts+ (Jonathan Lam)
why: Concrete steps for soft character and prop shadows (duplicate, Fill black, X-rotate 180 in 3D, align at the feet, Gaussian blur ~12, opacity ~60%, layer order); a quick stock recipe for grounding the host on a stage.

title: Matte effects (Matte Choker, Refine Soft Matte, Simple Choker)
author: Adobe Help Center
why: Edge treatment controls with exact behaviour: choke/spread, Refine Soft Matte edge detail, chatter reduction and decontaminate edge colors; cleans fringes and halos on cut-out characters before light wrap and shadows.

title: How To Light a Set for Animation with Adobe After Effects - A Scene Case Study | Animation Tutorial
author: Daniel Gies
why: Daniel Gies case study relighting a full animation set in AE: deciding light sources, painting light and shadow passes, color and mood per scene, whatever the asset quality; makes plain backdrops feel lit and gives the host a believable light to sit in.

title: Noise and Grain effects (Add Grain, Match Grain, Fractal Noise, Turbulent Noise)
author: Adobe Help Center
why: Exact controls for Add Grain/Match Grain (presets, intensity, size, channel balance, blend modes, final-output view) and Fractal/Turbulent Noise; the stock toolkit for grain, de-banding and procedural texture in the finishing pass.

title: Animated Grain shading in After Effects tutorial - Noise and textured gradients
author: Ben Marriott
why: Ben Marriott's animated grain shading: noise-based textured gradients and shading on flat vector shapes; adds the tactile, illustrated finish that makes clean shape-layer graphics feel crafted.

title: RGB Split in After Effects | Chromatic Aberration Tutorial
author: Ben Marriott
why: Ben Marriott builds RGB split / chromatic aberration in stock AE (Shift Channels-style channel separation, radial from frame center, kept subtle, expression-driven); a tasteful lens finish for hits and transitions.
